svg.title: A client arrives with right facial droop, slurred speech, and right arm drift that began about 40 minutes ago. Blood pressure is 168/94 mm Hg, blood glucose is 118 mg/dL, and the client is alert. NIHSS score is 12.
svg.desc: Because the deficits are ongoing at 40 minutes with a high NIHSS score of 12 (severe stroke), the client must be treated as an acute ischemic stroke rather than waiting to see if symptoms resolve into a TIA; a normal glucose of 118 mg/dL rules out a hypoglycemic cause, and there is no seizure history to suggest Todd's paralysis. A stat noncontrast CT and preparing for possible alteplase are the priority actions, since imaging must rule out hemorrhage before any thrombolytic or antiplatelet is given; giving aspirin before imaging or aggressively lowering blood pressure could worsen an undiagnosed hemorrhagic bleed or drop cerebral perfusion. Blood pressure (reporting over 185/110 mm Hg) and oxygen saturation (keeping above 94%) are the priority parameters, not potassium, uric acid, or ketones, which are unrelated to acute stroke monitoring.
